body:
## Context

Follow-up from the 1.11.0 release-audit pi/OpenCode blockers (containment shipped separately). Today every documented mutating recovery verb calls requireKeyOrExit (bin/handoff.mjs: write :137, resume :260, continue :548, supervise :718, bypass :850, repair :957) — except runUnlock (:1012), whose key posture is unverified. An operator without ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY whose repo carries an open deny has no documented escape beyond manual file deletion. Also, the recovery-exception command matcher (packages/context-handoff/lib/recovery-exception.mjs) — which lets a denied agent's shell at least REACH the recovery CLI under band — is wired only into claude-code and codex; pi and opencode have no matchRecoveryCommand reference at all.

## What to build

1. Verify runUnlock's key posture; make "unlock" a deliberately keyless, audited, deny-clearing verb (or build an equivalent), with the security analysis for why keyless unlock does not reopen the D1-D3 bypass surface (unlock clears the deny but does NOT mint resume authority — that stays key-gated).
2. Port the recovery-exception matcher into pi's tool_call path and opencode's tool.execute.before path so the recovery CLI is reachable under band.
3. Update every adapter's deny text to name the keyless verb.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A keyless operator can clear an open deny with one documented command and no manifest key, and the act is recorded. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs` exits 0 with a keyless-unlock test present.
2. pi and opencode allow the recovery CLI invocation under band. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/*.test.mjs plugins/adlc-opencode/test/*.test.mjs` exits 0 with recovery-exception tests present.
3. Resume/consume authority remains key-gated (negative test). verify: existing resume-auth tests stay green in the same runs.
title: context-handoff: key-free operator recovery — verify/ship keyless unlock, port the recovery exception to pi and opencode
